why: The daemon and the window's core each read participants' and groups' names: which machine a name is kept on, whether it is the human or Muster, and whom a question is asked of. The core depends on no daemon crate, so it spells these rules itself; both are run against these cases, so a rule cannot come apart between them unseen.

cases.name: a name with nothing after its last @ names no machine
cases.why: Both halves must be there: `@human+p2` is a pair group with the human, kept here, and `a@` and `@b` name nobody on any machine.

cases.name: a name kept on another machine splits at its last @
cases.why: `review@devenv` is the group `review` on `devenv`, and `@human@laptop` the human on `laptop`. A name splits at its last @, so `@human@laptop@x` is something on `x` whose own name is `@human@laptop`, which is not the human.

cases.name: the human and Muster are named exactly
cases.why: A name that starts like the human's is somebody else's, and so is one with an @ and no machine after it.

cases.name: a question is asked of the human when it names them or nobody
cases.why: A question addressed to the human, or to nobody, may be answered by the human; one addressed to others only may not, nor one the human asked. The human is named as the group's home names them: `@human` there, or `@human@laptop` in a group kept on another machine.
